newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-ALL EYES ON HINGIS AT HOPMAN CUP. [CORRECTED 13:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ALL EYES ON HINGIS AT HOPMAN CUP. [CORRECTED 13:36 GMT]

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis, fresh from her scintillating finish to the 1996 season, will be the focus of attention at the Hopman Cup mixed team event starting on Sunday.

Following the withdrawal of world number one Steffi Graf, the 16-year-old Hingis has the spotlight virtually to herself following a brilliant end-of-season run which took her to fourth in the world rankings. She starts the new year ranked sixth.
The right-handed Swiss reached her first grand slam quarter-final at the Australian Open last January to start a year she finished in a blaze of glory.

A semifinal berth at the U.S. Open in August was followed by four final appearances in her last five events. She collected her first singles title at Stuttgart in October and a month later humbled Monica Seles 6-2 6-0 to win the Oakland tournament.
In the end of season finale -- the WTA Championships -- Hingis pushed Graf to the limit before losing in five sets.

Hingis will partner Marc Rosset for Switzerland in the event which features eight (corrects from 12) countries split into two groups. Each tie comprises a men's and women's singles and a mixed doubles.

The second-seeded Swiss pair, who forfeited last year's final in embarrassing circumstances when Rosset injured his hand after hitting an advertising hoarding in a fit of rage, open their campaign on Monday when they meet tournament newcomers Romania.

Graf withdrew from the $640,000 competition on Friday due to a virus and has been told to stay in bed for five days but is expected to be fit for the Australian Open in Melbourne beginning on January 13. She has been replaced by Petra Begerow who will partner Bernd Karbacher.
The pair start against third-seeded South Africans Wayne Ferreira and Amanda Coetzer on Monday.
The tournament blasts off on Sunday when two of the game's biggest servers, Goran Ivanisevic of top seeds Croatia and Australia's Mark Philippoussis, come head-to-head.
Mary Pierce and Guy Forget of France take on Americans Chanda Rubin and Justin Gimelstob in the other match on Sunday.
